title: light-presubmit-prober-and-dependency-differ
author: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Add a lightweight presubmit prober ('presubmit-differ') that detects scope of dependency and toolchain changes to reduce install IO, and wire it into our presubmit workflow to route costly installs to staged lanes. Motivation: CI spend and noisy presubmit runs remain the largest drag on dev feedback cycles for infra-heavy changes. This PR implements a fast heuristic that compares lockfile deltas, package manifest deltas, and a small toolchain manifest to determine if a full toolchain bootstrap is required or if a cached partial layer suffices. Goals: - Reduce average presubmit install time for non-dep commits. - Prevent unnecessary full toolchain pulls on shallow changes (docs, tests, small code edits). - Provide observability (metrics) so SRE can tune thresholds. High level changes: - Introduce .github/actions/presubmit-differ/action.yml: composite action encapsulating the detection logic and exit codes for routing. - Add scripts/toolchain-bootstrap.sh: idempotent bootstrap that supports partial layer fetch by tag. - Add scripts/ci/cache-warmup.go: a small Go utility to probe remote cache and surface warm/cold state to CI. - Update .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: early presubmit step runs presubmit-differ and sets outputs to route to 'fastpath' or 'full' lanes. - Add docs/dev/presubmit.md with usage, metrics to watch, and rollback steps. - Minor Makefile/README tweaks to document new targets. Checklist: - [x] implement lightweight differ and composite action - [x] wire to presubmit workflow and staged lanes - [x] add cache probe utility and metrics emission to CI logs - [x] add docs and rollback plan - [x] performance validation on internal canary CI (see CI summary below) Performance observations (canary): - Median install time on fastpath reduced from ~42s to ~9s for non-dep commits. - Full-lane runs unaffected. - Cache probe reduces unnecessary full downloads by ~62% for the sampled week. Related: ENG-2048 (presubmit performance), SUP-912 (support ticket reporting flaky installs). Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag (this PR toggles flag via workflow inputs) 2) Canary: route 10% of PRs to the new router for 72 hours 3) Monitor presubmit latency and false-negative rate on cache detection 4) Gradual ramp to 100% and kill switch available in workflows Docs: docs/dev/presubmit.md includes both operator playbook and developer-facing notes. Backwards compatibility: If the differ action fails, workflow falls back to 'full' lane to be safe. No current breaking changes expected.
commits: feat(presubmit): add presubmit-differ composite action; feat(ci): add cache-warmup probe utility; feat(toolchain): partial bootstrap support and tagging; docs(presubmit): add presubmit.md; ci(workflow): wire presubmit-differ outputs into presubmit.yml; chore: add tests for cache probe; fix: idempotent bootstrap edge-case
discussion:
Ethan Liu (reviewer): Can the differ be gamed by maliciously updating lockfile comments or reordering entries? Response: The action hashes canonicalized lockfile contents (sorted keys + deterministic serialization) and normalizes ordering; minor reordering won't change the computed fingerprint. We also TTL signatures in the probe so an attacker would need to push a full change to affect routing.

Sofia Ramirez (reviewer): How do we observe false negatives (i.e., we route fastpath but the job actually needed full bootstrap)? Response: The probe emits a 'bootstrap_required' boolean and a 'confidence' float to workflow logs. We added metrics that increment on downstream install failures that trigger the 'fallback_full' path; dashboards are included in docs/dev/presubmit.md.

Liam O'Neal (reviewer): Are we adding any privileged network calls in the action? Security note: The composite action runs the probe and calls our internal cache API with a short-lived runner token scoped to cache:read; no credentials are persisted. Security reviewed by infra team (see SUP-912).

Author (Maya Patel): Addressed review comments: - improved canonicalization logic and added unit test (tests/presubmit/differ_test.go) - limited probe tokens to cache:read and added rotation instructions in docs - added conservative default: confidence threshold defaults to 0.9 to minimize false fastpath routing.

CI Maintainer (automation): First run failed due to flaky network to cache backend; reran job and all checks passed. CI summary: lint: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-presubmit: pass after rerun; e2e-canary: pass; security-scan: pass with low-severity notice (token scope checked).

Merge decision: After two approving reviews and successful canary smoke runs, approved for squash merge. Rollout toggled on 10% canary for 72h post-merge. If presubmit latency regresses or install failure rate climbs >1% absolute, we will roll back the router flag.
release_notes: Introduce presubmit-differ that reduces unnecessary full toolchain bootstraps by routing safe PRs to a fastpath; adds cache probe utility and documentation. Improves median presubmit install time for non-dependency changes.
notes_for_ops: Canary enabled: 10% of PRs for 72h. Monitor metrics: ci.presubmit.latency.p50, ci.presubmit.full_bootstrap_rate, ci.presubmit.fallbacks. Hook to alert: SRE oncall if fallback rate > 1% for 1h.
testing_summary: Unit tests for differ logic added (tests/presubmit/differ_test.go). Ran 3-day internal canary across ~1.2k PRs: fastpath hit-rate 58%, median presubmit time for fastpath 9s, regression none observed on full lane. Manual negative tests verified fallback when probe returns low confidence.
future_work: - Extend differ to consider transient devdeps via heuristics - Add de-duplication across monorepo packages to reduce repeated installs - Integrate with presubmit cost dashboard to show per-PR savings
notes: If an incident occurs related to presubmit routing, use rollback: flip presubmit-differ.enabled=false in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml and re-run CI.
